title: Planning an air quality project
context: A professor meets a student to review the plan for a group research project on air quality. The student is describing the plan for himself and his partner.

transcript.speaker: Professor Green
transcript.text: Come in, Anh. Tell me how your air quality project is going.

transcript.speaker: Anh
transcript.text: Chris and I have decided to compare air pollution in Bangkok and Hanoi. We've set up twelve sensors, and we've been collecting readings for three weeks.

transcript.speaker: Professor Green
transcript.text: Good. How often are the sensors taking measurements?

transcript.speaker: Anh
transcript.text: Every fifteen minutes. The problem is that two of the sensors stopped working when it rained, so we lost some data from last month.

transcript.speaker: Professor Green
transcript.text: That's frustrating, but it's common. Make sure you record the gaps in your report, because readers need to know where the data is missing.

transcript.speaker: Anh
transcript.text: We will. For the comparison itself, we'll use government air quality reports and our own sensor readings. We decided not to use social media posts, because they're too unreliable.

transcript.speaker: Professor Green
transcript.text: Sensible. Do you know how you'll present the results?

transcript.speaker: Anh
transcript.text: Chris wants to build a long video, but I think a simple chart is clearer. We'll present in three weeks, and we'll keep the talk to about twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: Professor Green
transcript.text: Twenty minutes is fine for a group. Could you send me the draft report?

transcript.speaker: Anh
transcript.text: Of course. The draft report is due on Wednesday, and we'll upload it to the shared folder that morning.

transcript.speaker: Professor Green
transcript.text: Good. We'll meet next Tuesday to review the charts. Where will you be presenting?

transcript.speaker: Anh
transcript.text: We've been told we'll present in room seven, on the second floor of the science building.
